gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-hind-vadodara: Stencilia leaves open gaps where its curves end, which gives it structure. Hind Vadodara carries the text in clean sans strokes of constant thickness, with tall, open-looking bowls that keep paragraphs easy to follow.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-kufam: Kufam reads like neon tubing, one track width and open curves. What stands out most is the split: Stencilia strikes with structural gaps at its curve ends while Kufam stays uniform and quiet.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-lexend: Approachable lowercase in Lexend runs large, with open jaws on every curve and thickness that holds steady around bends. Stencilia adds structural, striking gaps at its terminals, the sharpest contrast here.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-liter: Structural, striking, and full of gaps at the curve ends. That is Stencilia up top; Liter then runs on in uniform, nib-drawn strokes, wide-mouthed rounds keeping extended paragraphs moving smoothly.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-michroma: Structural and striking, Stencilia leaves generous gaps where its curves finish. Michroma gives each letter a wide berth, so tall-bodied lowercase with stubby ascender tips unspools slowly and spaciously across a page.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-montserrat-under: Striking from the first glance, Stencilia leaves spacious gaps at its curve terminals. Montserrat Underline handles the reading, with breathing counters and oversized lowercase whose round walls hold one width throughout.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-noto-sans-adlam: Stencilia strikes first, leaving spacious gaps where its curves end. Noto Sans Adlam then carries the text in clean sans-serif, with curve endings kept well apart, echoing that same openness.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-noto-sans-adlam-: Text in Noto Sans Adlam Unjoined reads with generous space between curve ends and stems, and little height difference between cases. Stencilia above adds structural, striking gaps of its own.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-noto-sans-anatol: Striking and structural, Stencilia leaves spacious gaps at curve ends. Noto Sans Anatolian Hieroglyphs reads modern, with outward-pointing terminal tips, its x-height rising close to cap height, so text runs on comfortably.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-noto-sans-bhaiks: Structural, striking letters up top: Stencilia leaves spacious gaps at its curve terminals. Noto Sans Bhaiksuki takes the text, its lowercase swollen like tightly coiled rope and its open apertures easy to make out.
